Figure 13 breaks down the test perplexity reduction by the number of constraints in each scenario, using the dense warmup schedule. DynaMiCS maintains a stable advantage over baselines from 3 to 7 constraints, while baselines degrade steadily and collapse to near-zero median reduction by 7 constraints. Only at 10 constraints, the most extreme tier where the model must simultaneously preserve performance on 10 heldout domains, DynaMiCS struggles as well, consistent with the inherent difficulty of satisfying that many preservation requirements at once (note, however, that solutions are still found for Qwen3-8B and Gemma312B).

Figure 1 DynaMiCS overview. Problem setup. Fine-tuning datasets D provide the data available for mixture selection, including target datasets and optional auxiliary datasets for transfer or regularization. Evaluation domains E are partitioned into target domains, whose losses are minimized, and constrained domains, whose losses must remain below reference values. DynaMiCS optimization. At each update, DynaMiCS estimates a slope matrix S(t) (1), where Sij(t) measures the local effect of training on dataset Dj on evaluation loss Li. Green/red entries denote loss decreases/increases. Given S(t), DynaMiCS solves a constrained optimization problem to obtain weights w∗ (2), trains with them for Ht steps (3), and then repeats the procedure. The simplex illustrates the proxy objective landscape, with white lines marking constraint boundaries; values are illustrative.

Figure 18 Evolution of dataset weights during training under a schedule of updates with dense warmup, for Qwen 3B, Qwen 8B, and Gemma 12B at LoRA rank 32. Weights are piecewise constant between controller recomputation steps.

Figure 14 shows the results. Across all model configurations, DynaMiCS consistently achieves lower violation than the best baseline, with a more concentrated distribution closer to zero. This indicates that the optimizer’s constraint-aware weight selection reduces forgetting even in scenarios where full constraint satisfaction is unattainable, a property that baselines, which have no mechanism to respond to constraint violations, cannot match.
